questions.question:
**Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Wasserkopf returns to his school and asks for a refund of his tuition fee.

B. ‘Refund’ by Karinthy is a hilarious play about a student named Wasserkopf.

C. However, the situation changes when the Mathematics teacher asks him to calculate the total amount.

D. He further declares that he had learnt nothing at school in all the years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BADC**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• **Sentence B **will be the starting line because it contains the main idea of the para jumble i.e. Refund(a play).
 
• **Sentence A** states that Wasserkopf returned to his school and asked for a refund of his tuition fee. So, **A** will follow **B**.
 
• Further,** Sentence D** states that he further declared that he was asking for a refund because he had learned nothing at school & **Sentence C **states that the situation changed when the Mathematics teacher asked him to calculate the total amount of his refund. So, **C** will follow **D**.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **B**: ‘Refund’ by Karinthy is a hilarious play about a student named Wasserkopf.
 
• **A**: Wasserkopf returns to his school and asks for a refund of his tuition fee.
 
• **D**: He further declares that he had learnt nothing at school in all the years.
 
• **C**: However, the situation changes when the Mathematics teacher asks him to calculate the total amount.

 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** *‘Refund’ by Karinthy is a hilarious play about a student named Wasserkopf. Wasserkopf returns to his school and asks for a refund of his tuition fee. He further declares that he had learnt nothing at school in all the years. However, the situation changes when the Mathematics teacher asks him to calculate the total amount.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

How many languages do you learn at school?

options.text: How many languages will you learn at school?
Languages are learnt by how many at school?
How many languages are learnt by you at school?
How many languages have you being learnt by you learning at school?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'How many languages are learnt by you at school?'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• In 'active-passive' transformation except for (who and whom) rest of the Wh-family Pronouns will remain unchanged. 
 
• Here in the given question 'How many languages' will remain unchanged.
 
• 'do learn' will be changed into 'are learnt'. 
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be added. **
 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__ *How many languages are learnt by you at school?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

• परिवर्तन की प्रक्रिया इस प्रकार है:
 
 
• 'Active-Passive' परिवर्तन में **(who और whom)** को छोड़कर शेष Wh- परिवार pronouns अपरिवर्तित रहेंगे।
 
• यहां, दिए गए प्रश्न में 'How many languages' अपरिवर्तित रहेंगी।
 
• 'do learnt**' को 'are learnt' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
 
• अंत में, preposition 'by' जोड़ा जाएगा।

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

6 +12 × 8 ÷ 16 - 12 = 8
questions.solution:
According to the BODMAS rule:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

**Option 1 :** - and +

Given:

6 + 12 × 8 ÷ 16 - 12 = 8

After interchange the signs;

6 - 12 × 8 ÷ 16 + 12 = 8

By BODMAS rule

6 - 12 × 0.5 + 12 = 8

6 - 6 + 12 = 8

18 - 6 = 8

12 = 8** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

**Option 2 : **+ and ×

Given: 

6 + 12 × 8 ÷ 16 - 12 = 8

After interchange the signs;

6 × 12 + 8 ÷ 16 - 12 = 8

By BODMAS rule

6 × 12 + 0.5 - 12 = 8

72 + 0.5 - 12 = 8

72.5 - 12 = 8

60.5 = 8** (LHS ≠ RHS)**

**Option 3: **× and ÷

Given:

6 + 12 × 8 ÷ 16 - 12 = 8

After interchange the signs;

6 + 12 ÷ 8 × 16 - 12 = 8

By BODMAS rule

6 + 1.5 × 16 - 12 = 8

6 + 24 - 12 = 8

30 - 12 = 8

18 = 8 **(LHS ≠ RHS)**

**Option 4: **÷ and +

**Given:**

**6 + 12 × 8 ÷ 16 - 12 = 8**

**After interchange the signs;**

**6 ****÷ 12 × 8 + 16 - 12 = 8**

**By BODMAS rule**

**0.5 × 8 + 16 - 12 = 8**

**4 + 16 - 12 = 8**

**20 - 12 = 8**

**8 = 8 (LHS = RHS)**

Hence, the answer is **“****÷ and +”.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 27 days and 54 days, respectively. They completed the work in 9 days with the help of C. How many days will C take to complete eight-ninths of the work alone?

A and B can complete a piece of work in 27 days and 54 days, respectively.

Work = efficiency × time

**Calculation:**

Efficiency of B = 54/54 = 1 unit/day

**∴ The correct answer is 16 days.**

__Shortcut Trick__

By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle subtended by that chord in the alternate segment.

⇒ ∠PBC = ∠BAC = 65°

⇒ ∠PCB = ∠BAC = 65°

In ΔBPC, the sum of all interior angles is 180°:

⇒ ∠BPC + 65° + 65° = 180°

⇒ ∠BPC = 180° − 130° = 50°

**Given:**

ΔABC is inscribed in a circle with center O.

**Calculations:**

⇒ The angle subtended by chord BC at the circumference is ∠BAC = 65°.

⇒ The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly double the angle subtended at the circumference.

⇒ Central Angle ∠BOC = 2 × ∠BAC = 2 × 65° = 130°.

⇒ The radius drawn to the point of contact is directly perpendicular to the tangent line.

⇒ Therefore, ∠OBP = 90° and ∠OCP = 90°.

⇒ In quadrilateral OBPC, the sum of all internal angles is strictly 360°.

⇒ ∠BOC + ∠OBP + ∠BPC + ∠OCP = 360°

⇒ 130° + 90° + ∠BPC + 90° = 360°

⇒ 310° + ∠BPC = 360°

⇒ ∠BPC = 360° − 310° = 50°

**∴ The correct answer is 50°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Segment Theorem

The angle between a tangent line and a chord passing through the point of contact is perfectly equal to the angle subtended by that same chord in the alternate segment of the circle.

Angle Between Intersecting Tangents

The angle between two distinct tangents drawn from an external given point to a circle is supplementary to the central angle subtended by the chord connecting their respective points of contact (∠P + ∠O = 180°).

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle strictly subtended by an arc at the center is mathematically double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle's circumference.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**200 crores**__.

• **Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks (UCBs)**, which are desirous of voluntarily converting into small finance banks, may refer to the Scheme on the voluntary transition of Urban Co-operative Bank into a Small Finance Bank.

 
 
• UCBs applying for transiting to small finance banks or obtaining in-principle approval for such transition (under the above-referred scheme), will be required to ensure compliance with these ‘on tap’ licensing guidelines from the date of commencement of business as small finance bank except the guideline on minimum capital.
 
• The minimum net worth of such small finance banks shall be Rs.100 crore from the date of commencement of business.

• The objective behind these is to provide financial inclusion to those sections of the economy which are not being served by other banks, such as small business units, small and marginal farmers, micro and small scale industries and institutions in the unorganized sector.

questions.question: Who among the following begun his excavations at Dholavira in 1990?

• The ancient site at Dholavira was first discovered by Jagat Pati Joshi in 1966-68, and excavated almost two decades later by a team led by R.S. Bisht in the 1990s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dholavira **was discovered in 1968 by the archaeologist Jagatpati Joshi.

 
 
• ** Excavations of the site between 1990 and 2005 under the supervision of archaeologist R S Bisht** revealed the ancient city, which was a commercial and manufacturing centre for about 1,500 years before its collapse and eventual ruin in 1500 BC.
 
• Dholavira is one of the two most notable excavations of the Indus Valley Civilization or Harappan culture, dating back to 4500 years ago.
 
• While the second site, Lothal, is more elaborately educated and easier to access, a visit to Lothal only complements rather than replaces a visit to Dholavira.
